chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants in His decree and judgment, but He is Just in His decree and judgment.
And He is not unjust to them in His decree and judgment, but He is Just in His decree and judgment.

key_terms.قَضَاء: Decree or divine determination of affairs

ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology define Allah's justice in relation to His decree and judgment?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirming that Allah’s decree (qada') and judgment (hukm) are rooted in absolute justice ('adl), a core tenet of Shia theology that distinguishes divine action from arbitrary will. This narration reinforces the belief that God’s actions are never unjust to His servants, countering the Mu'tazila and Akhbari views on divine compulsion or caprice. It underscores the theological principle that every divine act, whether perceived as good or bad by humans, is inherently just and wise.
